ai.text:
This proposal sets up a framework for collecting and publishing non-financial statistics on commercial real estate across the EU. Policymakers need such data to make economic and monetary decisions, to watch for risks to the financial system, and to guide macroprudential policy. Past financial crises showed that trouble in property markets can seriously harm the financial system and the wider economy, and the European Systemic Risk Board found large gaps in comparable information on commercial property prices, rents and construction starts across countries. At present there are few official sources for this kind of data, and policymakers mostly buy it from private organisations.

The proposal would fill that gap by covering five kinds of information: building permits (the number of dwellings and usable floor area), construction starts and work completions (usable floor area), commercial real estate price indices, rent indices, and the value of transactions. The list can be changed later through delegated acts. The proposal also sets quality standards and reporting rules, describes what Member States and data holders must provide and what access they have, and allows the Commission to set further data details and simplified requirements, taking into account the size of each country's market. Pilot studies can be run before any new data requirements are adopted, and EU budget grants can fund the work.

The European Parliament would decide on the proposal under the ordinary legislative procedure, on equal footing with the Council. The financial impact is open-ended, with a start-up period from 2026 to 2028. Funding for 2026 and 2027 would come from existing programme allocations, with total appropriations estimated at EUR 3.6 million, and later funding depends on the next multiannual budget agreement.
